title: Invention of Cuneiform Writing in Sumer
summary: Sumerians in Mesopotamia develop the world's earliest known script using wedge-shaped stylus marks on clay tablets to record economic transactions and royal decrees.

title: Unification of Upper and Lower Egypt by Narmer
summary: Pharaoh Narmer (Menes) unifies the Nile Valley kingdoms into a centralized state, establishing the First Dynasty and the pharaonic institution.

title: Construction of the Great Pyramid of Giza
summary: Pharaoh Khufu commissions the colossal Great Pyramid of Giza, representing the pinnacle of ancient stone engineering and religious devotion to the afterlife.

title: Establishment of the Akkadian Empire by Sargon
summary: Sargon of Akkad unifies the diverse city-states of Sumer and Akkad, creating the world's first historically documented multinational empire.

title: Promulgation of the Code of Hammurabi
summary: King Hammurabi of Babylon carves 282 edicts on an eight-foot basalt stele, establishing explicit civil penalties and proportional justice across Mesopotamia.

title: Battle of Kadesh and First International Peace Treaty
summary: Ramesses II of Egypt clashes with Muwatalli II of the Hittite Empire in Syria, culminating in the earliest known bilateral mutual defense and peace treaty in history.

title: Inauguration of the Ancient Olympic Games
summary: The first recorded Olympic athletic contest is held at the sanctuary of Olympia in honor of Zeus, establishing a pan-Hellenic sacred truce (Ekecheiria).

title: Traditional Founding of Rome
summary: Legendary founding of the city of Rome on the Palatine Hill by Romulus, initiating Roman political identity from monarchy to world empire.

title: Constitutional Reforms of Solon in Athens
summary: Lawgiver Solon abolishes debt slavery (Seisachtheia) and restructures Athenian citizenship based on economic wealth rather than aristocratic lineage.

title: Establishment of the Roman Republic
summary: The Roman patricians expel King Tarquinius Superbus, replacing monarchical autocracy with elected consular magistracies and the authority of the Senate.

title: Greco-Persian Wars (Marathon and Salamis)
summary: Allied Greek city-states withstand two successive Persian imperial invasions, securing the autonomy of Greek culture and democratic Athens.

title: Periclean Golden Age of Classical Athens
summary: Under the visionary leadership of Pericles, Athens witnesses flourishing democratic participation, philosophical inquiry, dramatic arts, and the building of the Parthenon.

title: Enactment of the Roman Law of the Twelve Tables
summary: Rome's earliest statutory code is displayed publicly in the Forum, guaranteeing plebeians equal access to legal rights and procedural justice.

title: Trial and Execution of Socrates
summary: Athenian jurors condemn philosopher Socrates to death by hemlock for allegedly corrupting the youth and defying the traditional gods, immortalized by Plato's Apology.

title: Founding of Plato's Academy in Athens
summary: Plato establishes his school outside the walls of Athens, creating the prototype for Western universities where philosophy, mathematics, and science were taught.

title: Conquests of Alexander the Great
summary: Alexander leads Macedonian forces across Egypt, Persia, and into the Punjab, shattering the Achaemenid Empire and propagating Hellenistic culture across Afro-Eurasia.

title: Punic Wars: Rome Overcomes Carthage
summary: Three protracted wars between Rome and maritime Carthage culminate in the total destruction of Carthage, leaving Rome the undisputed hegemon of the Mediterranean basin.

title: Julius Caesar Crosses the Rubicon
summary: Julius Caesar marches his XIII Legion across the Rubicon boundary into Italy with the declaration 'Alea iacta est', precipitating the civil war that destroyed the Republic.

title: Establishment of the Roman Empire and Pax Romana
summary: Octavian is bestowed the title Augustus by the Senate, establishing the Principate and initiating two centuries of institutional stability and imperial prosperity.

title: Inauguration of the Colosseum in Rome
summary: The Flavian dynasty completes the massive concrete and stone amphitheater in central Rome, showcasing Roman architectural engineering and civic spectacles.

title: Edict of Milan: Legalization of Christianity
summary: Emperors Constantine I and Licinius proclaim freedom of religion throughout the Roman Empire, ending state persecutions and transforming Christianity into a dominant world faith.

title: Fall of the Western Roman Empire
summary: Germanic general Odoacer deposes the last Western Roman emperor Romulus Augustulus, marking the traditional transition from classical antiquity to the Middle Ages in Europe.

title: Neolithic Agricultural Revolution
summary: Hunter-gatherers transition to permanent agrarian settlements through the domestication of plants and animals, enabling surplus food and the rise of complex civilizations.

title: The Scientific Revolution
summary: Emergence of modern empirical science, driven by heliocentrism, analytical mathematics, and the experimental method from Copernicus to Isaac Newton.

title: The Industrial Revolution
summary: Transition to new manufacturing processes powered by steam engines, mechanized textile looms, metallurgy, and railroads, radically reshaping human society.
